name: What Counts as Evidence
title: What Counts as Evidence
description: Evidence is verifiable fact relevant to the decision: test data, measurements, analysis results, standard clauses, supplier certifications. Opinions, habits, and 'we always do it this way' are not evidence.
how_it_works: For each decision, list candidate evidence and grade it (direct measurement beats analogy; current data beats old). Cite the evidence concretely - document, page, test ID - so anyone can re-check it.
key_points: Evidence: test data, measurements, analysis, standards, certifications.
Not evidence: opinion, habit, precedent alone.
Grade evidence by directness and currency.
Cite concretely: document, page, test ID.
requirements: Defined decision with options considered; evidence artifacts (data, analysis, test results); recorded rationale and approver.
standards: Decision-record practice (ADRs - architecture decision records); engineering change control documentation standards.
citations: Architecture Decision Records (ADR) practice - Michael Nygard's documented pattern.
INCOSE decision management process guidance.

One page forces clarity; appendices hold detail.
Approver and date make it accountable.
Short records get read; long ones get filed unread.

name: Options Must Be Real
title: Options Must Be Real
description: A decision between one real option and strawmen is theater. Honest records show genuine alternatives with their evidence - including the option of doing nothing.
how_it_works: Develop at least two viable options plus the null option (do nothing / keep current), and give each a fair evidence summary. If only one option is viable, record why the others failed.
key_points: At least two viable options plus the null option.
Strawmen are theater, not engineering.
Record why rejected options failed.
Fair summaries even for the losers.
requirements: Defined decision with options considered; evidence artifacts (data, analysis, test results); recorded rationale and approver.

Future engineers need the why, not just the what.
Honest weak links beat hidden ones.

name: Approvers and Accountability
title: Approvers and Accountability
description: Every decision needs an approver with authority to own the consequences. Unowned decisions drift; owned decisions get the attention their impact deserves.

key_points: Authority matches impact: bigger decisions, higher approvers.
Record approver and date on every decision.
Approvers own consequences and answer future questions.
Rubber stamps are not approvals.

description: Evidence varies in strength: measured data outranks simulation, which outranks analogy, which outranks opinion. Grading evidence prevents weak proof from carrying big decisions.

key_points: A: measurement, B: validated analysis, C: analogy, D: opinion.
Bigger decisions demand stronger evidence grades.
State grades in the record - no hidden weakness.
Weak evidence can inform; it should rarely decide alone.

name: Trade Study Method
title: Trade Study Method
description: A trade study compares options against weighted criteria with scored evidence - the formal version of 'pros and cons'. Weights come from stakeholders; scores come from evidence.
how_it_works: Define criteria and weights with stakeholders, score each option per criterion from evidence, and compute weighted totals. Sensitivity-check the weights: if small changes flip the winner, the decision is fragile.
key_points: Criteria and weights from stakeholders; scores from evidence.
Weighted totals rank the options.
Sensitivity-check weights for decision fragility.
Document the study - the numbers are the rationale.
requirements: Defined decision with options considered; evidence artifacts (data, analysis, test results); recorded rationale and approver.

title: Decision Timing Under Uncertainty
description: Decisions have last-responsible moments: decide too early and you decide on fog; too late and options expire. Good timing is itself a decision discipline.
how_it_works: For each pending decision, define what information would change it and when that information arrives; decide at the last moment the information still allows. Reversible decisions go early; irreversible ones wait for data.
key_points: Define what info would change the decision and when it arrives.
Last responsible moment: not early, not late.
Reversible decides early; irreversible waits for data.
Timing is a decision - manage it deliberately.
requirements: Defined decision with options considered; evidence artifacts (data, analysis, test results); recorded rationale and approver.
standards: Decision-record practice (ADRs - architecture decision records); engineering change control documentation standards.

key_points: Two-way doors: decide fast, adjust later.
One-way doors: decide slow, with heavy evidence.
Most decisions are more reversible than feared.
Match process weight to reversal cost.

name: Cognitive Biases in Build Decisions
title: Cognitive Biases in Build Decisions
description: Sunk cost, confirmation bias, anchoring, and optimism distort build decisions systematically. Naming them in the process is the defense - bias thrives in unnamed darkness.
how_it_works: Build bias checks into decision reviews: ask what evidence would change the choice (confirmation), separate past spend from future choice (sunk cost), and get independent estimates (anchoring). Pre-mortems surface optimism.
key_points: Sunk cost: past spend must not drive future choice.
Confirmation: ask what evidence would change your mind.
Anchoring: get independent estimates before sharing yours.
Pre-mortems counter optimism with imagined failure.

standards: Decision-record practice (ADRs - architecture decision records); engineering change control documentation standards.

description: Decision reviews - did the evidence hold up? did the choice work? - turn experience into organizational learning. Unreviewed decisions teach nothing.
how_it_works: Schedule reviews of major decisions after outcomes are known, compare actuals to the evidence-based predictions, and update templates and checklists with lessons. Blame-free: the target is the process.
key_points: Review major decisions after outcomes are known.
Compare actuals to evidence-based predictions.
Update templates with lessons learned.
Blame-free: fix the process, not the person.
requirements: Defined decision with options considered; evidence artifacts (data, analysis, test results); recorded rationale and approver.
standards: Decision-record practice (ADRs - architecture decision records); engineering change control documentation standards.
citations: Architecture Decision Records (ADR) practice - Michael Nygard's documented pattern.

The log is organizational memory; curate it.

name: Quantitative Decision Analysis
title: Quantitative Decision Analysis
description: Expected value, decision trees, and Monte Carlo turn uncertain choices into quantified bets. When stakes are high, quantify - gut feel does not scale to millions.
how_it_works: Model options as decision trees with probabilities and payoffs, compute expected values, and check sensitivity. Use where the analysis cost is small relative to the stakes.
key_points: Decision trees with probabilities and payoffs.
Expected value ranks options under uncertainty.
Sensitivity analysis tests the ranking's robustness.
Quantify when stakes dwarf analysis cost.
requirements: Defined decision with options considered; evidence artifacts (data, analysis, test results); recorded rationale and approver.
standards: Decision-record practice (ADRs - architecture decision records); engineering change control documentation standards.

name: Ethical Dimensions of Build Decisions
title: Ethical Dimensions of Build Decisions
description: Build decisions affect safety, environment, workers, and communities - ethics belongs in the decision record, not just in compliance checkboxes. Stakeholder impact is evidence too.
how_it_works: Include affected-party impact in options analysis, apply the precautionary principle where harm is plausible, and document ethical reasoning alongside technical. Escalate ethical concerns through defined channels.

Document ethical reasoning with the technical.

name: Decision Debt
title: Decision Debt
description: Deferred and evidence-poor decisions accumulate as decision debt - choices that must be revisited, with interest paid as rework. Track it like technical debt.
how_it_works: Log deferred decisions with their trigger conditions and evidence gaps, review the debt register regularly, and pay it down before interest (rework) compounds. Make debt visible to management - invisible debt never gets paid.
key_points: Deferred/evidence-poor decisions are debt with interest.
Log triggers and gaps; review regularly.
Pay down before rework interest compounds.
Visible debt gets paid; hidden debt bankrupts.
requirements: Defined decision with options considered; evidence artifacts (data, analysis, test results); recorded rationale and approver.
standards: Decision-record practice (ADRs - architecture decision records); engineering change control documentation standards.
citations: Architecture Decision Records (ADR) practice - Michael Nygard's documented pattern.

name: The Decision Audit Trail
title: The Decision Audit Trail
description: Regulated and high-stakes builds need complete audit trails: every decision, its evidence, approver, and timestamp, retrievable years later. The trail is the proof of diligence.
how_it_works: Maintain immutable decision logs with evidence links, control access and changes, and retain per regulatory or contractual periods. Test retrievability - an archive you cannot search is a write-only memory.
key_points: Immutable logs: decisions, evidence, approvers, timestamps.
Retain per regulatory/contractual periods.
Test retrievability regularly.
The trail proves diligence years later - keep it complete.
